I'm attaching a pre-filled W-8BEN-E and their company registration doc for your review. If Redwood requires additional confirmation (EIN, or US payee set-up), let us know and we can propose an alternate US payee (NOVA US LLC) — that would require an updated invoice from the US entity.

Can we get an outline of what Redwood needs to release the outstanding $46,200?

Hi Sophie — appreciate the quick response and the attachments. A few clarifying points so we can route this correctly in AP: 

1) Because NOVA is a UK entity and the invoice came from NOVA Analytics Ltd (no US EIN), Redwood needs a completed W-8BEN-E with an accompanying proof of company registration and bank details to validate foreign payee status. The W-8BEN-E needs to be signed and dated.

2) If NOVA intends for Redwood to issue 1099s (US reporting), we would instead need the US subsidiary to invoice (W-9 + EIN). Otherwise, no 1099 will be issued for a foreign entity.

3) Our compliance team has a specific W-8BIN/E intake flow (we use DocuSign for signatures). I can send the DocuSign link if you prefer to sign the form there — it helps speed verification.

Next steps: Please confirm whether you will: (A) submit a signed W-8BEN-E and bank details for NOVA UK, or (B) re-issue the invoice from NOVA US LLC with a W-9. If (A), upload the signed form here or sign via DocuSign (link below). If (B), please confirm the US payee legal name and EIN.

DocuSign (recommended): https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abc-123-efg

I'll mark this urgent — AP has put a hold on the payment until we complete entity classification.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Accounts Payable Specialist
Redwood Inference

Hi Sophie — looping in Legal for treaty/withholding guidance. Quick answers: 

- Redwood can pay an international GBP account via wire. Our AP prefers USD where possible but we support SWIFT/GBP deposits. Please include IBAN/SWIFT on the remit form.
- If NOVA signs a W-8BEN-E and claims treaty benefits, standard procedure is to have Legal review the treaty line items; absent a treaty claim, payments to foreign entities for services performed outside the US are generally not subject to US withholding. We need the completed W-8BEN-E to confirm.

Rishi — can you confirm whether a treaty claim is appropriate based on the submitted documents? If you need more detail from the vendor (e.g., place of effective management, where services were executed), call it out and we'll ask them.

Best,
Markus Klein
Finance Manager, Redwood Inference

Hi Sophie — thanks for the prompt turnaround on the W-8BEN-E (we received the signed copy via DocuSign). A few requests to finalize: 

1) Please confirm the primary place where the consulting services were delivered (country/city) and whether any personnel billed to Redwood are US-based. This helps us determine treaty applicability.
2) Can you upload the vendor bank details on the Remit_Instructions form (IBAN, SWIFT, account name). We need that to initiate the SWIFT payment.
3) We will not withhold US tax if the services were performed outside the US and a valid W-8BEN-E is on file without a treaty reservation. If NOVA claims a treaty benefit, indicate which article and attach supporting docs.

Once we have the signed W-8BEN-E (received), place-of-performance confirmation, and bank details, AP will push the wire. Expected release: within 3 business days after complete documentation.

If you prefer a phone call to close this faster, I'm available Mon/Tue 9–12 PT.

Regards,
